originalTitle: Egypt want officials kicked out of World Cup
title: Egypt Says 'No Fair!' in Big Football Game
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends all across Africa! It's your friendly news reporter, here to tell you about some exciting (and a little bit tricky!) news from the world of football. We love football, don't we? It's a game where teams run, kick, and try to score goals. It's so much fun to watch and play!

What Happened in a Big Game?

Imagine two big countries, Egypt and Argentina, playing a very important football match. A match is like a big game where two teams play against each other to see who is the best! Well, Egypt played Argentina, and Egypt lost the game. Oh dear! Losing can be a little sad, but it's part of the game. But something else happened that made the people from Egypt feel unhappy. They felt like the game was not played fairly. When we play games, we always want them to be fair, right? Like when you share toys with your friends, you want everyone to get a fair turn. It's the same in football!

Who Are the Referees?

In every football game, there are special grown-ups called 'referees' or 'officials'. Their job is super important! They are like the teachers in a classroom or a grown-up making sure everyone follows the rules when you play. Referees make sure all the players follow the rules of football. They blow whistles, they show yellow or red cards, and they decide if a goal counts or not. They must be very, very fair to both teams. They can't like one team more than the other. That would not be right! Did you know? Referees have to run a lot during a game, sometimes even more than the players! They need to be very fit!

What Did Egypt Say?

After the game where Egypt lost to Argentina, the people in charge of Egypt's football team were not happy. They thought the referees did not do a good job. They felt that the referees were not fair to their team. They thought the referees treated Argentina better than Egypt. This is called 'double standards'. It means treating two different groups of people in different ways, even when they do the same thing. Imagine if you and your friend both played with a ball. If you threw the ball too far and got told off, but your friend threw the ball too far and didn't get told off, that wouldn't be fair, would it? That's what Egypt felt happened. They felt the referees used 'double standards' – being harder on Egypt and easier on Argentina for the same things. They were so unhappy that they decided to make a 'complaint'.

What is a Complaint?

A 'complaint' is like when you tell your parents or teacher that something is not fair. You say, 'Excuse me, I don't think that was right!' Egypt's football team made a complaint to a very important group called 'FIFA'. Did you know? The word 'FIFA' comes from French words, but it's easier to think of it as the 'World Football Boss'!

Who is FIFA?

FIFA is like the 'big boss' of all football in the whole wide world! They make sure everyone plays by the same rules, no matter where they are from. They organize big, exciting football tournaments, like the famous World Cup. The World Cup is where the best teams from different countries play to see who is the champion of the world! Did you know? FIFA was started a very, very long time ago, in 1904! That's even before your grandparents were born! When Egypt made their complaint, they sent it to FIFA. They asked FIFA to look into what happened.

What is an 'Investigation'?

When someone asks FIFA to 'investigate' something, it means FIFA will look very, very closely at everything that happened during the game. It's like being a detective! They will watch the game videos again and again. They will ask questions to the referees and the teams. They want to find out the truth: did the referees really make unfair calls? Was it really 'double standards'? Egypt wants FIFA to find out if the referees were fair. If they weren't fair, Egypt wants those referees to be 'kicked out' of the World Cup. This means Egypt wants those referees to not be allowed to be in charge of any more big games, especially not in the World Cup. It's like saying, 'If you can't be fair, you can't play this important role anymore!'

Why Is This Important?

This news is important because it reminds us all about 'fair play'. Fair play means everyone follows the rules and everyone gets a fair chance. It makes games fun and exciting for everyone. When games are fair, it makes sure that the best team wins because of their skills, not because of unfair decisions. Did you know? In many sports, players shake hands before and after a game to show good sportsmanship and fair play! Even if you are playing with your friends in the park, remembering to be fair makes the game much more enjoyable for everyone. So, FIFA will now look very carefully at the game. We hope they find out the truth and make sure football is always fair for everyone. Remember, whether you win or lose, playing fair is the most important thing! Keep kicking those balls and having fun, my friends!
summary: The country of Egypt thinks the referees were not fair in a big football game against Argentina and has asked the big boss of world football, FIFA, to check what happened.
whyMatters: It's important because everyone deserves a fair chance to play and win, and rules help make sure sports are fun and fair for everyone.
